389	  wNeeds && { label: 'W-fix', wt: A.wt.W, model: T.opus,
390	    prompt: `In W (branch b10/W). Blocking findings ${JSON.stringify(blocking(ck['W-review']))}. ` + FIX_COMMON },
391	].filter(Boolean)
392	const fixedRaw = await parallel(FIXES.map(f => () => agent(COMMON(f.label, f.wt) + f.prompt,
393	  { label: f.label, phase: 'Fix', model: f.model, effort: 'high', schema: IMPL })))
394	const fixed = await settle(FIXES, fixedRaw, IMPL, null)
395	
396	// ---------- Gate: one build, every run once, on the merged result ----------
397	phase('Gate')
398	const parts = [done.W && 'b10/W', CB.length && 'b10/K', LB.length && 'b10/L'].filter(Boolean)
399	const GATE = (tree, from) => COMMON(tree + '-gate', A.wt.M) + `${from}
400	Then, on that one build: ant compileAll (runlog), restore global.map, library compile in order. Launch at once, detached: the
401	distance (run.sh, scratch under ${S}) and ant testFast. When testFast ends: ant testSystem, then the checker count
402	(checker-count/run.sh), then the 85 programs of explorations/compile-ladder/baseline-2026-09-19/pass-list.txt (compile and run,
403	two at a time). Poll every 4 minutes at most. Collect: both suites (0 failures; counts against the base's 1,782 and 504 plus the
404	new tests; testSystem as the sum of its four shards); the pass list; the checker count; the distance by kind, class and crash,
405	with per-site deltas against the base and against L (${S}/tools/mapline.py): C's clears, and the unmasked errors inside the four
406	crashed declarations, apart from caused ones. Green iff both suites have no failures and the pass list holds; the measurements are
407	reported, never red. Return RUN.`
408	let gate = await agent(GATE('M', `Seed ${A.wt.M} as branch b10/M; merge ${parts.join(', ')} (--no-ff). Stop on any conflict that
409	is not two disjoint edits of one region (Appendix I is the likely place); commit.`),
410	  { label: 'M-gate', phase: 'Gate', model: T.sonnet, effort: 'medium', schema: RUN })
411	if (!gate) gate = await agent(RECOVER('M-gate'), { label: 'M-gate-status', model: T.sonnet, effort: 'low', schema: RUN })
412	if (!gate || gate.verdict !== 'green') {
413	  log('Gate red: one fix, one re-gate')
414	  await agent(COMMON('M-fix', A.wt.M) + `In M (branch b10/M). The gate: ${JSON.stringify(gate)}. Attribute each failure to its piece
415	(W: walk evaluator; C: checker; G, N: library) and repair it. ` + FIX_COMMON,
416	    { label: 'M-fix', phase: 'Gate', model: T.opus, effort: 'high', schema: IMPL })
417	  gate = await agent(GATE('M2', `M (branch b10/M) now holds M-fix's commits on top of the gated merge; do not merge again.`),
418	    { label: 'M2-gate', phase: 'Gate', model: T.sonnet, effort: 'medium', schema: RUN })
419	  if (!gate || gate.verdict !== 'green') return { ready: false, reason: 'gate red twice: the director decides', gate, missing }
420	}
421	
422	// ---------- Finish ----------
423	phase('Finish')
424	const labels = IMPLS.map(p => p.label).filter(l => done[l]).concat(FIXES.map(f => f.label), ['M-fix'])
425	const fin = await agent(COMMON('finish', A.wt.M) + `The gate is green at code id ${gate.codeId}: ${JSON.stringify(gate)}.
426	1. Reports: concatenate ${R}/C-infer.md, C-decl.md and C-crash.md into ${R}/C.md; keep W.md, G.md, N.md; write ${R}/REPORT.md
427	   (what each piece did; distance base 340, then L, then M, by kind, class and crash, read through the per-site lists; what the
428	   crash repairs unmasked; the checker count; the suite counts) and ${R}/gate/summary.txt (code id, commands, counts, verdicts).
429	2. Ledger: from ${S}/status/{${labels.join(',')}}.json apply every close, note and new row. Take the ledger from origin/main as it
430	   is now (git fetch), not from the base, and number new rows from its last row.
431	3. Make branch b10/land at origin/main. Bring in from b10/M every path changed in ${A.base}..b10/M except the ledger, plus the
432	   reports and the applied ledger. If origin/main changed any of those paths since ${A.base}, stop and report it. One commit
433	   naming the four pieces, with the session's attribution lines.
434	4. sameCodeAsGated = (code id of b10/land) == ${gate.codeId}. Return FIN. Do not push.`,
435	  { label: 'finish', phase: 'Finish', model: T.sonnet, effort: 'medium', schema: FIN })
436	return { ready: !!(fin && fin.sameCodeAsGated), fin, gate, missing,
437	         reviews: { W: ck['W-review'], C: ck['C-review'], Lib: ck['Lib-review'] } }
438	```
439	
440	### After the script (the coordinator)
441	
442	If `ready`, the coordinator adds the `FACTS.md` correction (the written bound `Object`) to the
443	landing commit; it is an `explorations/` edit, so the code id does not change. Then it runs
444	`git push origin b10/land:main`. If `origin/main` moved before the push, it rebases. If the
445	rebase leaves the code id unchanged, it pushes; the gate's result is reused under rule 3.
446	If not, it runs the Gate and Finish phases again on the new base. It then removes the ten
447	worktrees and the scratch runs, after checking `git worktree list`.
448	
449	### The agents at a glance
450	
451	| Agent | Tier, effort | Reads | Prompt in one line | Output |
452	|---|---|---|---|---|
453	| W | Opus, high | brief W, section 4 entries, rows 544/534/588/425/584/585, OverloadedFunction, BuildEnvironments, EvaluatorBase, checker precedents, spec passages, Park extract | promote three tests, write two, see them fail; load refusals for 534 and 544 scoped to keep String loading; upper bound for 588; testSystem once; S1 text | branch b10/W, W.md, IMPL |
454	| C-infer | **Fable**, high | brief C (593, 604), Functionals, Types, NodeUtil, NonPrimitive:229, functions.tex, inference.tex | probe the varargs type on the compiled path first; promote two tests, write the owed ones; repair applicability, body type, inference; S1 callout and new entry | b10/C-infer, C-infer.md, IMPL |
455	| C-decl | Opus, high | brief C (563, 574, 605, 597), AbstractMethodChecker, OverloadingChecker, TypeHierarchyChecker, objects.tex, traits.tex | renaming apart, message, field binding, object expression against `comprises`, each test first | b10/C-decl, C-decl.md, IMPL |
456	| C-crash | Opus, high | base distance output, the four crashed declarations, the checker code the traces name | trace each crash, minimal program, row, repair only small and only in owned files, else hand over | b10/C-crash, C-crash.md, IMPL |
457	| G | Opus, high | brief G, base per-site list (57), the G sections of FortressLibrary .fss/.fsi, precedents | value test first; repair each site by the library's own device or leave it with a row; testSystem once | b10/G, G.md, IMPL |
458	| N | Opus, high | brief N, base per-site list (60 + 18), N's sections, List, FortressBuiltin, Writer, RangeInternals | the drop; 590, 602 promoted; the 60 sites; value test; testSystem once | b10/N, N.md, IMPL |
459	| K-launch | Sonnet, low | the three C branches | seed K, merge, build once, testFast detached | RUN (launched) |
460	| L-launch | Sonnet, low | G, N branches | seed L, merge, no build, distance detached | RUN (launched) |
461	| W-review | Opus, high | W diff, W.md, runlog, spec passages | refute against the overloading and inference rules, Conversions, S1 form | REVIEW |
462	| C-review | Opus, high | K diff, C-*.md, runlog | refute: principled repairs, harness keys, S1 form; owner per finding | REVIEW |
463	| Lib-review | Opus, high | L diff, G.md, N.md, runlog | refute against Library practice, exclusion rule, ownership, walk values | REVIEW |
464	| K-collect | Sonnet, medium | runlog, TEST-RESULTS | wait for testFast, report failures | RUN |
465	| L-collect | Sonnet, medium | distance output, base per-site list, diff | per-site delta with lines mapped; write the line mapper | RUN |
466	| C-fix / Lib-fix / W-fix | Opus, high (C-fix Fable when C-infer's work is blocked) | collector and review results, handed-over patches | repair test first, no suite rerun | IMPL |
467	| M-gate | Sonnet, medium | the three group branches | merge, build once, testFast, testSystem, pass list, checker count, distance with deltas | RUN |
468	| M-fix, M2-gate | Opus high; Sonnet medium | the red gate | only if red: one repair, one re-gate | IMPL; RUN |
469	| finish | Sonnet, medium | status files, reports, origin/main's ledger | reports, gate summary, ledger rows, one squashed commit, code-id check | FIN |
470	| *-status | Sonnet, low | one status file | only on an empty return | the stored result |
471	
472	### Why this shape and not another
473	
474	- **Batches, not pipelines.** The workflow guidance defaults to `pipeline()`. Here,
475	  though, the two-slot cap makes the total agent time the bound on wall time, whatever
476	  the shape. And a resume replays only the longest unchanged prefix of calls in call
477	  order. In a pipeline the order of later calls depends on timing, so after a restart,
478	  agents that had finished would run again: for a 2-hour implementer, that means hours of
479	  tokens and rebuilt code states. A batch issued at once fixes the order. Its cost is the
480	  tail of each batch, about 0.4 h in Build when the jobs are ordered longest first.
481	- **C in three agents, split by file.** As one agent, C would take about 4 to 5 hours and
482	  carry a context of more than 500 k tokens. Split by the files each part owns, the three
483	  merge without conflict. The one shared hot spot is `NodeUtil.getParamType`, which raises
484	  both row 604's type and crash 1's "Type is not inferred". It is given to C-infer, and
485	  C-crash hands its patch over.
486	- **G and N each one agent.** Their sizes are similar (about 60 sites). Splitting either
487	  would double the orientation reading and leave an odd number of jobs for two slots.
488	- **One distance run per group, not per agent.** A run takes 20 minutes. One run on L
489	  (the library against the base's checker) gives the attribution the brief asks for. M
490	  gives the rest: C's effect is M minus L, and the crash-unmasked errors fall inside
491	  declarations that no library piece owns. So no separate run on K is needed.
492	- **Ledger and row numbers in one place.** Four pieces opening rows in one table would
493	  collide, and other workers commit too. Rows are therefore numbered once, at landing,
494	  against `origin/main`.
495	
496	## 3. How correctness is assured, and where checking pays
497	
498	**The layers, in the order they act:**
499	
500	1. **Test first, recorded, never repeated.** Each fix's test is committed before the fix
501	   and run on the seeded base build. The run log records its code id and verdict.
502	   Reviewers check the order of runs from the log; they do not rerun, which rule 3 would
503	   forbid. Promoted tests are seen failing as plain tests. Owed pins (the lone-parameter
504	   pin, G's and N's value tests) are seen passing before the change and after it.
505	2. **Each piece's own runs.** Each piece runs its own tests and the must-keep tests the
506	   brief names, one at a time (about 8 s for a walk test, about 5 s for a compile). W, G
507	   and N run testSystem once on their final code: 4 minutes covers every library load and
508	   every walk test, and those three pieces are the ones that can change them.
509	3. **Group runs.** K runs testFast once, because C is the only piece that touches the
510	   compiler. L runs the distance once, which shows each library repair's effect against the
511	   base's checker. It also finds the two failures that no walk test shows: a site that was
512	   meant to clear and did not, and an error that a repair caused.
513	4. **Independent review.** There are three reviews, one per group. They are adversarial
514	   and run on Opus, each with a checklist made from the binding decisions. They cover the
515	   judgement rules that no test checks:
516	   - the library's own device, with no cast round the checker;
517	   - Conversions: nothing changes which declaration runs;
518	   - the S1 form and Appendix I's six parts;
519	   - the harness's semantics of `XXX`;
520	   - ownership.
521	5. **The merged gate.** testFast and testSystem run with zero failures, and the counts
522	   must be the base's plus the new tests (testSystem as the sum of its shards). The
523	   85-program pass list must hold. The checker count and the distance are reported with
524	   deltas. Errors the crash repairs unmask are kept apart from errors a repair caused.
525	6. **Landing.** The landed commit's code id must equal the gated one. Otherwise the code
526	   is gated again.
527	
528	**Where checking is worth its cost:**
529	
530	- **The merged gate.** Required by rule 2. About 30 minutes of machine time and about
531	  110 k tokens.
532	- **testSystem in W, G and N.** About 4 minutes and a few thousand tokens of polling each.
533	  W's new load checks reach every type that walk loads. Without this run, a false refusal
534	  would surface only at the gate, where it costs a fix agent and a 30-minute re-gate.
535	- **testFast on K.** 11 minutes, which overlap the reviews. Changing the varargs typing
536	  and inference could break compiled tests in many places. Catching that before the merge
537	  keeps the cause attributable to C alone and avoids a red gate.
538	- **The distance on L.** 20 minutes, which overlap the reviews. The brief asks for this
539	  reading. It is also the only check on the library repairs' real target, the checker's
540	  error list.
541	- **The three reviews.** About 0.45 M tokens in all. The library rules ("the library's own
542	  device", "never a cast", "no walk value change") and the S1 form are what this step
543	  could get wrong in ways no suite would show. A wrong device lands green and becomes
544	  precedent.
545	
546	**Where checking is not worth its cost:**
547	
548	- **Panels of several skeptics per finding.** The verdicts here come from tests and
549	  measurements. A review finding is cheap to act on and is checked again at the gate.
550	- **A distance run per agent, or one on K.** 20 minutes of a core each. The L run and the
551	  M run attribute everything that is needed.
552	- **testFast per C agent.** Three times 11 minutes on four cores. Once on K is enough,
553	  because the three agents own disjoint files.
554	- **testSystem on L.** G and N each ran it, they own disjoint declarations, and M runs it
555	  again.
556	- **Reviewing the runners.** Their output is machine output with internal sums to check
557	  (shards add up, deltas balance). A wrong parse shows up as an inconsistency at the gate.
558	- **A separate S1-form checker.** The W and C reviewers read the same text; it is folded
559	  into their checklists.
560	- **Re-running anything to confirm.** Forbidden by rule 3, and the run log makes that
561	  mechanical.
562	
563	## 4. The estimate
564	
565	**Agents:** 18 expected.
566	
567	- The minimum is 15: 6 implementers, 7 in Check, the gate and the finisher, with no
568	  fixes and no recoveries.
569	- The maximum is about 23: all three fixes, the re-gate pair and three status readers.
570	
571	**Tokens written,** in the cost the project counts (cache writes and new input). An
572	agent writes about 11 k in its first message, and then roughly its final context, if its
573	cache never lapses.
574	
575	| Role | Agents | Tokens written | Assumption |
576	|---|---|---|---|
577	| Implementers | W 220 k, C-infer 280 k (Fable), C-decl 230 k, C-crash 250 k, G 300 k, N 320 k | 1.60 M | Context sizes come from what each reads: about 12 to 15 tokens per source line (W reads about 3,500 lines; G and N about 2,500 to 3,000 library lines plus messages), plus tool output and about 40 to 60 k of its own edits and notes. |
578	| Reviewers | W 110 k, C 150 k, Lib 180 k | 0.44 M | Each reads a diff (about 300 to 1,200 lines), the reports and the cited passages. |
579	| Fixers | C 180 k, Lib 170 k, W 0.3 × 120 k | 0.39 M | C and Lib are likely needed; W only on a blocking finding (probability about 0.3). |
580	| Launch, collect, gate | K-launch 40 k, L-launch 35 k, K-collect 50 k, L-collect 70 k, M-gate 110 k, M2-gate 0.35 × 90 k | 0.34 M | Small prompts, polls of about 1 k each, parsing. |
581	| Gate fix | 0.35 × 180 k | 0.06 M | A red first gate, probability about 0.35. |
582	| Finisher | 100 k | 0.10 M | Composes reports, applies about 25 ledger changes. |
583	| Coordinator (main session) | | 0.11 M | Phase 0, the launch, reading the result, landing. |
584	| Contingency | | 0.25 M | One lapsed cache on a large agent (about 250 k) or a few status readers. |
585	| **Total** | | **≈ 3.3 M** (range 2.5 to 4.5 M) | Fable's share is 0.28 M, or 0.46 M if C-fix escalates. |
586	
587	**Wall time,** at an Opus implementer's pace of about 25 to 35 s per tool round trip and
588	120 to 200 round trips:
589	
590	| Stage | Wall | How it is reached |
591	|---|---|---|
592	| Phase 0 | 0.25 h | Seeding takes 3 s a worktree. If the base must be built: about 200 s. A base distance, if needed, runs detached during Build. |
593	| Build | 4.9 h | Six jobs, longest first, on two slots: N 2.2, G 1.8, C-infer 1.5, C-crash 1.5, W 1.2, C-decl 1.2. A slot sits idle about 0.4 h at the tail. A C iteration costs about 2.6 min (rebuild about 40 s, library compile 110 s, one compile 5 s). |
594	| Check | 1.1 h | The launchers take 10 and 5 min. The reviews take 25, 35 and 35 min. The collectors start after the reviews, when testFast (about 16 min under load) and the distance (about 24 min under load) have finished. |
595	| Fix | 0.75 h | Two fixers in parallel, about 45 min each. |
596	| Gate | 0.75 h | Build and library compile take about 3.5 min. The distance runs alongside testFast, then testSystem, the checker count and the pass list (85 × about 6 s, two at a time), about 31 min of machine time in all, plus merging and parsing. |
597	| Re-gate | 0.4 h expected | 1.2 h with probability 0.35. |
598	| Finish and land | 0.5 h | |
599	| **Total** | **≈ 8.6 h** (7 to 11) | The two-slot cap sets it: total agent time is about 14 h, so 14 / 2 plus the single-slot tail of the gate and finish. |
600	
601	At 8.6 h, a run that starts more than about 4 hours into the session's 13-hour life will
602	meet the stop. The design resumes from the journal: finished agents keep their results,
603	and the unfinished ones continue from their status files and branches. Each restart
604	still costs about the in-flight agents' contexts written again (0.2 to 0.6 M tokens).
605	
606	## 5. What I would want measured or decided before running it
607	
608	**Decisions for the director:**
609	
610	1. **Rule 1 for library slips (G and N).** Rule 1 asks for a failing test in the corpus
611	   before every edit of the original tree. A compiled-checker error on the one library
612	   cannot be held by any test the harness runs today: the compiled corpora check
613	   `CompilerLibrary`, and the measurements are report-only by decision ("Count never red").
614	   The brief's own tests for G and N pass before and after. I propose this reading: the
615	   base per-site list is the failing evidence for a library site, recorded by code id, and
616	   the walk value test is the test kept. That reading needs his word. The script passes it
617	   in as `libraryEvidence`.
618	2. **Row 604's third face against the library route.** `Types.IMMUTABLE_HEAP_SEQ_NAME` is
619	   resolved from `WellKnownNames.fortressLibrary()` when the class loads. On the compiled
620	   path that is `CompilerLibrary`, and none of `CompilerLibrary`, `CompilerBuiltin` or
621	   `CompilerAlgebra` declares `ImmutableArray` (checked by grep). Nothing may be added to
622	   the prelude. So a compiled test of the positive program (a varargs parameter used as a
623	   sequence in its body) probably cannot pass before the switch-over. Is the over-acceptance
624	   test enough for this step, with the positive program held by a row? C-infer is told to
625	   probe and report rather than route round it. The answer changes C-infer's scope.
626	3. **The scope of W's Meet Rule over symbolic operators.** `String`'s four families pair
627	   `(a:Any, self)` with `(self, b:Any)`, the shape the rule refuses, and the brief requires
628	   that they keep loading. The likely way is to skip symbolic operators as the checker does
629	   (row 584). That gives walk the same blind spot on purpose. Confirm, or name another way.
630	4. **Partial landing.** If one piece is blocked, may the other three land (the script's
631	   default), or does the step land whole or not at all?
632	5. **Commit shape.** I propose one squashed commit for the step, as the finisher builds it,
633	   with no untested intermediate states on `main`. The alternative is one commit per piece
634	   plus an integration commit: easier to read in the history, but only the last state is
635	   gated. Also confirm the report paths (`explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-10/`, with
636	   `gate/summary.txt` there).
637	6. **The Fable budget.** C-infer needs about 0.3 M tokens of Fable, or about 0.46 M if the
638	   C fixer escalates. Is that available this week, or should C-infer run on Opus at its
639	   highest effort?
640	
641	**Measurements (each a few minutes, none on the critical path):**
642	
643	7. **Whether a `nohup setsid` job outlives the agent that started it.** The
644	   launch, review and collect overlap depends on it. If it does not, the launchers must
645	   hold their slots until the run ends, which adds about 0.5 h.
646	8. **Whether the distance measurement can run on one unit** (for example `FortressLibrary`
647	   alone, 732 s of the 1,212). If it can, G and N could check their own sites before they
648	   return, and L's fix round would shrink or disappear.
649	9. **One C iteration on this machine:** Scala rebuild, library compile, one compiled test.
650	   I assumed about 2.6 minutes. If it is more than about 4 minutes, the C agents should
651	   batch several rows per rebuild.
652	10. **The base's reusable evidence.** Is there a gate summary and a distance per-site list
653	    (with the run's output, for C-crash's traces) whose code id is the base's? If not, one
654	    distance run goes into Phase 0.
655	11. **The session's uptime** against the stop at 46,636 s. Free disk: ten worktrees at
656	    206 MB each, plus parser directories at 5.8 MB per grammar-importing run.
657	12. **The harness's slot order.** That `parallel()` with more thunks than slots starts them
658	    first in, first out, in array order. Both the longest-first ordering and the
659	    reviews-before-collectors overlap depend on it.

content.content:
100:- **No re-measuring what the record holds.** "you are wasting resources on remeasuring." A brief hands over what the record has measured as findings to cite and names the one new thing to measure; a clean worker is clean of our options, not of our measurements (protocol principle 5). A rung whose test is the checker-count or distance stage takes the last landed gate's tables as its before and does not re-run the stage on an unchanged base; the gate commits its per-site list so that the before is complete. The nine steps are a way to brief him on unfamiliar ground, a type-theoretical question answered from the theory, the rule and a few declarations; and one global rule is sought from type theory and the peers' implementations rather than a rule slapped on a rule ("I cannot be trusted to derive a rule that wouldn't break the whole system and be a hodgepodge of edge cases").
101-- **Reversible stops do not hold a batch.** A stop a batch record reserves for him (a model or APL line beyond the approved ones, an interpreter output a rung cannot account for): "These don't need me now. They are reversible things I can review later. Don't block start of next batches on these." It lands, the push and the next batch go ahead, and it is listed for his review (the protocol's first hard rule). An output difference the untouched tree already shows from run to run, the test's verdict unchanged, is not a stop but a ledger row ("we had a rule too stringent because the spirit of the test is still held"); a rung's small items go to the ledger for review, not to him one per message.
102-- **A blocking second review does not hold a green batch.** "we have enough rigor or robustness and backup in our processes after that, so that small failure in a rule should not be blocking ... landing large ships like this." After its one repair round, a merged-diff review that still blocks does not hold a batch whose gate is green: the batch lands, the review's remaining findings go to the next batch and are listed for his review, and the post-batch review follows. A red gate after its repair still stops a batch. Built into `coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js` and its manual. The merged-diff review itself stays inside the batch, once, beside the gate, as the check of the merged tree's records, the stops and the routing before the push; removing it and moving its checks to the review after the batch is not taken (Fable's review of the batch practice against the Opus review's; he sided with Fable).
103-- **A tests-only repair does not rerun the gate.** "we are being overly pedantic for no good reason with like how the gates are set up ... we have to be weighing costs and benefits and we are not skipping the test, we are adding the test, we are moving stuff to following batches, we are running reviews after the fact, so we will catch stuff that the rerunning of a gate is not." A repair after the gate that changes no source, library, checker, interpreter or specification file runs its new tests in the harness on the merged tree; the first gate's tables stand; the landing records the new tests beside them; a repair that changes code reruns the gate. The same weighing of cost against what a rule protects applies to every rule of the batch workflow. Built.
104-- **What a batch commits.** "the commit discipline in a branch should not be different from what you will be committing to the main. Like don't keep temporary shit around. We are backing up the transcripts anyway from all the workers. So if we need to dig up something, how the worker arrived at some point, we have the full transcripts." A worker commits, on its own branch as on `main`, only what `main` is to hold: the Fortress change, its tests, its report, the lines for the ledger, FACTS and the plan, and a script or tool that is reusable ("If that script that batch contributes a script that is reusable, it goes in there", such as the documented way of running the checker as a shadow); no captured outputs, logs, raw outputs, script copies or other scratch are committed anywhere; new issues go to the ledger, reports into the batch's report; the process, and whether a worker wrote its test first and saw it fail, is read from the workers' transcripts, which the backup keeps. Deleting the `wip/` branches after a gate is his own chore in the GitHub web page, and he is not reminded of it. Built into the script, its manual and the protocol.
105-- **Workers commit their own files as they go.** "Workers should be committing themselves as they go, focused their files only. Protects against container failures and stops from harness bothering you about uncommitted files." They push to their own `wip/` branches as they work; the wip branches are cleaned up after the gate; the workflow script lives in the repository, not only in a session; the coordinator pushes `main` every few minutes ("I hope we are committing as we go because I worry that the container will get reset"). A protocol hard rule.
106-- **Which tier runs what.** "You can spend as much Opus workers as you want." The highest-risk decisions touch all three of specification, interpreter and compiler, which may disagree, and the design intent has to be inferred from the breadcrumbs left in all of them; the cheaper tier gathers the evidence into a condensed brief, and the high-level judgement of what makes sense given all the signals and what design balance lets the project grow belongs to the top tier, because that is the work it is for. Workers are pinned to Opus by the alias, "to make that workflow future proof"; the expensive model is escalated only at decision points, "sparsely so that it doesn't have to gather all the context by running multiple tool calls". Sonnet is the tier for archaeology. Two workers launched on the wrong tier once cost him 1.7 million tokens "down the drain". The coordinating session runs on Opus, so that Fable's own weekly pool is kept "for more important work"; it moves to Fable at his word when the pool on all models is spent, and how the Opus trial is judged is in `coordinator/postmortem-2026-09-27-record-keeping.md`.

### Count never red

Source: `explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md`, the entry titled "The checker count is measured, never red."

> **The checker count is measured, never red.** The checker-count measurement is reported with every full check of the tree and is never red on its own; the full distance measurement (all apis and components) is report-only, and its job is driving the error list down.

### Changes recorded

Source: `explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md`, the entry titled "Every change to the specification is recorded with its reason."

> **Every change to the specification is recorded with its reason.** "our plan needs to update the spec with the change that we do and somehow properly record why we decided that way, so that there is no open discrepancy between the spec and our implementation that would be confusing to people. We need to preserve the original historic record somewhere in a document with our reasoning why we did the switch and preserve the option to go the route C." Every change takes the S1 form, an original-tree edit flagged as such; `Specification-1.0-frozen/` is never touched.

### S1 form

Source: `explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md`, the entry titled "The S1 form"

> **The S1 form**, the layered form the team used for 1.0 and its 2009 draft: a labelled callout at each changed passage that prints in every build (not a `\note`); a revival section in Appendix I (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex`), each entry with the reason, the original sentences quoted with their path and line in the unrevised copy, and route C with what reversing to it would take; one paragraph in the front matter; the full reasoning in a repository document. The unrevised copy is called "the Working Draft of February 2011", in the team's own form, each citation giving the path and line in `Specification-1.0-frozen/`; Appendix I says once that the directory's name is misleading, since only `fortress.1.0.pdf` in it is the 1.0 release. So both designers knew the pipeline's shape in part: worker, skeptic, one repair, merge, gate. The experiment shows best what each would change in that shape, not what each would invent from nothing.

3The blind rerun

At your word the experiment ran again, blind: a new brief that says only what batch 10 must achieve, and two new designers, one on Opus and one on Fable Study.

What its brief held

  • Three new files, written by a Sonnet worker from batch 10's record Study:
    • content.md: the step's aim, its terms, the four pieces W, C, G and N (the rungs under another name) with their defects, files and what done means, who owns which declaration, and the binding decisions, 19 entries quoted from POSITIONS Blind brief;
    • requirements.md: your rules, five of them: test first, both suites green on the merged result, nothing built or run twice, only what main is to hold committed, every language change written into the specification Blind brief;
    • machine.md: the machine and its prices, checked against FACTS Blind brief.
  • The designers read only that, the source, the specification, the ledger and explorations/repo-internals.md Study. Each design says so in its header Blind Fable header Blind Opus header.

What was removed

  • Every pipeline word Study. None of the three files says rung, skeptic, judge, gather, gate, batch or worker Blind brief.
  • Every past cost Study: no batch 9 cost by stage, no 6M to 7M estimate for batch 10 Rec §1, no "past batches wrote about 6M to 8M" Brief.
  • The record and the files around it. The designers did not open the record, POSITIONS, FACTS or the build-cache note. The brief restates what they need from them.
  • The tier rule. The first brief bound Opus for workers, Sonnet for archaeology, Fable for judgements (section 2). machine.md says only that three tiers exist: Fable the strongest, on its own scarcer weekly pool; Sonnet the cheapest Blind brief.
  • One file too many. The rule against pipeline words also left out the file that holds the last per-site list of the distance measurement Study. Both designs ask where it is Blind Fable §5 Blind Opus §5.

The leak that remains: CLAUDE.md

  • CLAUDE.md reaches every agent. No brief can hold it back Study.
  • It names the collaboration protocol, the coordinator's plan and knowledge base, and the folder of the gate summaries, explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-*/gate/summary.txt. It calls the two suites "the gate for every change".
  • It shows. Both blind designs put their report in explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-10/, with a gate/summary.txt Blind Fable §5 Blind Opus §5. The ledger, which they read, names such folders too.
  • It names none of the pipeline's roles (worker, skeptic, judge, gather) and no token cost.

Tiers: the designers' own choice

  • No rule told them which tier runs what. Both chose a mix of all three.
  • Blind Fable put Fable on the three implementers whose edit restates a rule every test depends on, Opus on judgement over much reading, Sonnet on everything mechanical Blind Fable §1.
  • Blind Opus put Fable on one implementer, the checker part where a wrong repair is least visible to tests, Opus on judgement, Sonnet on every launch, collection, gate and landing Blind Opus §1.
  • Both put Fable on implementers, where your rule pins workers to Opus, and Sonnet well beyond archaeology POSITIONS. Section 5 gives each choice with its reasons.

So the blind two show what each designer builds from the content alone, short of what CLAUDE.md lets through.

Estimate: about 4.3M on Opus (3.0M to 6.4M), up to 0.2M on Fable, about 0.1M on Sonnet. 10 Opus agents and the measure in the base case, about 12 expected, 17 at worst. About 9.5 to 10 hours (8 to 12) Opus §4.

5Side by side, role by role

Both estimates are predictions, worked out by arithmetic from batch 9's figures. Neither is a measurement Fable §4 Opus §4.

Both put the largest part of their saving in the tail. Fable: the tail falls from 1.56M to about 0.5M, about 1.1M of its 1.7M below batch 9's 6.88M Fable §4. Opus: 0.8M of the 1.3M it assigns to stages comes from the tail; it puts its total saving at about 2M Opus §4.

input.new_string:
Estimate: about 4.3M on Opus (3.0M to 6.4M), up to 0.2M on Fable, about 0.1M on Sonnet. 10 Opus agents and the measure in the base case, about 12 expected, 17 at worst. About 9.5 to 10 hours (8 to 12) Opus §4.

The blind Fable design

Shape: four chains, one per piece, each in its own worktree on its own branch. A chain is a run of sub-pieces, each one implementer followed by a checker: nine in all, W one, C three, G two, N three. Why so fine: one context per piece "would pass 300,000 tokens"; nine stay near 150,000 to 250,000 Blind Fable §1.

Before the chains a Sonnet base agent reuses the base build or builds it (about 200 s), seeds the four worktrees, and stops if the base's per-site list is missing Blind Fable §2. Order: the chains run through the harness's pipeline(), so both slots stay busy, with no wait until all four end Blind Fable §1.

Tiers, its own choice Blind Fable §1:

  • Fable for W, C-a and C-b, "the three agents whose edit restates a rule every test depends on".
  • Opus for C-c and the five library repairers, "whose work is judgment over much reading"; also the reviewers, the integrator and the report writer.
  • Sonnet "for everything mechanical: verification by checklist, running suites, reading measurements, the S1-form check".
  1. ImplementerFable ×3Opus ×6×9

    Works in its chain's worktree after the sub-piece before it. Runs each test in the untouched worktree first and keeps the output as a record outside the repository; only then edits. W and C rebuild after their own edits (25 to 40 s); G and N build nothing. One commit: tests, fix and specification text. It runs no suite and no distance, and returns its ledger lines instead of editing the ledger Blind Fable §1, §2.

    Estimate: 1.35M on Fable, about 450K each; 2.4M on Opus, about 400K each Blind Fable §4

  2. Checklist verifierSonnet×9, about 4 more to re-verify

    Reads the diff and the records; runs nothing. Eight items: the paths touched, no team test changed, the test's failure seen in its record before the fix, each library hunk in its piece's declarations, no cast round the checker, the S1 form, the ledger lines, the report. "Cheap, mechanical, high yield" Blind Fable §2, §3.

    Estimate: 0.9M, 13 at about 70K Blind Fable §4

  3. Semantic reviewerOpus×3: W, C-a, C-b

    Reads the Java and Scala diff beside the passages, and asks whether the code states exactly the rule: not wider, not narrower. Builds and runs nothing. Only these three, because "a three-vote adversarial panel is not [the right price], because the suites are a stronger refuter than a second reader" Blind Fable §3.

    Estimate: 0.4M, about 130K each Blind Fable §4

  4. Fixupthe implementer's tierabout 4, up to 2 more

    After a verifier's or a reviewer's issue: one more commit, test first. A re-verify follows a verifier's fixup. A library chain whose sites survive its distance run gets one more pass Blind Fable §2.

    Estimate: 0.7M, about 120K each, 2 on Fable and 4 on Opus Blind Fable §4

  5. Gate runnerSonnet, low effort×7

    At each chain's end: testSystem for all, testFast for C, the distance for C, G and N. Once on the merged tree: both suites and both measurements. Never builds. A lock keeps two suites from sharing the four cores Blind Fable §1, §2.

    Estimate: 0.35M, about 50K each Blind Fable §4

  6. ReaderSonnet×6

    Maps each base site of the per-site list through the diff to the declaration it is in, and never reads the class table, which misfiles after an insertion (row 577). Reports what cleared, what survived and what appeared Blind Fable §2.

    Estimate: 0.5M, about 80K each Blind Fable §4

  7. IntegratorOpus

    Cherry-picks the four branches, in the order W, C, G, N, onto main's tip in a fifth worktree. Resolves conflicts by the brief's ownership map. Writes all ledger lines once, numbering new rows from 609, and builds once Blind Fable §2.

    Estimate: 250K Blind Fable §4

  8. Report writerOpus, medium effort

    After the merged gate: the batch report and the gate summary, tables only, no raw output Blind Fable §2.

    Estimate: 170K Blind Fable §4

  9. Base and final checkSonnet, low effort×2

    The base agent above. The final check reads the landing commit for rule 4, and pushes main only when you have set it to Blind Fable §2.

    Estimate: 50K and 40K Blind Fable §4

Not in it: a judge or ruling of any kind, and a review of the merged tree. A red gate, at a chain's end or on the merged tree, stops the run for you Blind Fable §2, §3.

Estimate: about 7.1M (5.5M to 8.5M): Fable about 1.6M, Opus 3.6M, Sonnet 1.9M. About 48 agents in its table, 46 in its text (40 to 52). About 13 hours, so "the run will meet the 13-hour stop once"; it resumes from the journal Blind Fable §4.

The blind Opus design

Shape: six implementers at once, each in its own worktree; then group runs in the background with three reviews beside them; a fix only where something was found; one gate on the merged tree; one commit Blind Opus §1.

Before the launch the coordinator, in about 15 minutes, builds or reuses the base, seeds six worktrees, and reuses the last gate result and per-site list when their code is the base's; otherwise the distance runs once, in the background Blind Opus §1.

The run log keeps rule 3, nothing built or run twice. It holds one line per build or run, keyed by a code id, a hash of the tree's source folders. An agent looks its command up first: "a finished result there is your result" Blind Opus §2.

Order: the six issued at once, longest first: N, G, C-infer, C-crash, W, C-decl. Batches, not a pipeline, so that a resume after the 13-hour stop replays the same calls Blind Opus §2.

Tiers, its own choice Blind Opus §1:

  • Fable for C-infer only: "Its rows have a decided type that collides with the library route, and the place to fix row 593 is unmeasured. This is where a plausible but wrong repair is most likely and least visible to tests."
  • Opus for the other implementers, the reviewers and the fixers, "whose work is judgement".
  • Sonnet for every launch, collection, gate, finish and recovery: "Their work is mechanical, their contexts are small, and their waits are long, so a lapsed cache costs little."
  1. ImplementerOpus ×5Fable ×1×6

    W, G, N, and C split by the files each part owns: C-infer (rows 593 and 604), C-decl (563, 574, 605, 597's checker half), C-crash (the four crashes). As one agent, C "would take about 4 to 5 hours and carry a context of more than 500 k tokens" Blind Opus §1, §2.

    Test first: committed, run once on the base build, seen failing, then the fix. Only its own tests and the named must-keep tests; W, G and N run testSystem once on their final code, the C parts no testFast. It never edits the ledger Blind Opus §1.

    Estimate: 1.60M, 220K to 320K each; C-infer's 280K on Fable Blind Opus §4

  2. LauncherSonnet, low effort×2

    K merges the three C branches, builds once and starts testFast in the background. L merges G and N, builds nothing, since no source changes, and starts the distance in the background Blind Opus §1.

    Estimate: 40K and 35K Blind Opus §4

  3. ReviewerOpus×3

    One for W, one for C on K, one for the library on L, while those runs go. Tries to refute, from a checklist made of the binding decisions. Reruns nothing; reads in the run log that each test failed before its fix Blind Opus §1, §2.

    Estimate: 0.44M Blind Opus §4

  4. CollectorSonnet×2

    Reads K's testFast, and L's per-site list against the base's, lines mapped through the diff. Each site goes to its owner; a site a report said would clear and did not is listed as missed Blind Opus §2.

    Estimate: 50K and 70K Blind Opus §4

  5. FixOpusat most one per group

    Only where a run or a review found something; on Fable for C when a blocking finding is C-infer's. Test first. No suite rerun, "because the merged gate is the rerun" Blind Opus §1, §2.

    Estimate: 0.39M expected Blind Opus §4

  6. GateSonnet

    Merges W, K and L into M and builds once. Runs the distance beside testFast, then testSystem, the checker count and the 85 programs of the compile ladder's pass list. Red: one Opus fix and one more gate; red twice stops for you Blind Opus §1.

    Estimate: 110K; a red gate expected at a 0.35 chance Blind Opus §4

  7. FinisherSonnet

    Writes the reports and the gate summary. Applies every ledger change, new rows numbered against origin/main at that moment. Makes one squashed commit whose code id must equal the gated one. Does not push: the coordinator adds the FACTS line and pushes Blind Opus §1, §2.

    Estimate: 0.10M Blind Opus §4

  8. Status readerSonnet, low effortonly on an empty return

    Reads back an agent's status file when the harness returns nothing for it Blind Opus §1.

    Inside the contingency Blind Opus §4

Not in it: a judge or ruling of any kind, a second skeptic, and a review of the merged tree Blind Opus §2.

Estimate: about 3.3M (2.5M to 4.5M), counting 0.11M of the coordinator's own work and 0.25M of contingency; Fable 0.28M, or 0.46M if the C fix goes to Fable. 18 agents expected (15 to 23). About 8.6 hours (7 to 11) Blind Opus §4.

6Side by side, role by role

How the four designs and the pipeline differ in shape

  • The pipeline: per rung a worker and a skeptic, and on a refusal a judge, a repair and a second skeptic; then a gather, a merged-diff review, a gate and a commit. Batch 9: 6.88M B9 §7.
  • The first two trimmed it: the same chain per rung with fewer checkers and rulings, and a thinner tail. About 5.2M, and about 4.3M on Opus Fable §4 Opus §4.
  • The blind Fable splits the work finer: nine implementers in four chains, a Sonnet checklist after each, the suites and the distance at each chain's end, then one merge and one gate. About 48 agents and 7.1M Blind Fable §4.

Shape: four chains, one per piece, each in its own worktree on its own branch. A chain is a run of sub-pieces, each one implementer followed by a checker: nine in all, W one, C three, G two, N three. Why so fine: one context per piece "would pass 300,000 tokens"; nine stay near 150,000 to 250,000 Blind Fable §1.

Before the chains a Sonnet base agent reuses the base build or builds it (about 200 s), seeds the four worktrees, and stops if the base's per-site list is missing Blind Fable §2. Order: the chains run through the harness's pipeline(), so both slots stay busy, with no wait until all four end Blind Fable §1.

Tiers, its own choice Blind Fable §1:

  • Fable for W, C-a and C-b, "the three agents whose edit restates a rule every test depends on".
  • Opus for C-c and the five library repairers, "whose work is judgment over much reading"; also the reviewers, the integrator and the report writer.
  • Sonnet "for everything mechanical: verification by checklist, running suites, reading measurements, the S1-form check".
  1. ImplementerFable ×3Opus ×6×9

    Works in its chain's worktree after the sub-piece before it. Runs each test in the untouched worktree first and keeps the output as a record outside the repository; only then edits. W and C rebuild after their own edits (25 to 40 s); G and N build nothing. One commit: tests, fix and specification text. It runs no suite and no distance, and returns its ledger lines instead of editing the ledger Blind Fable §1, §2.

    Estimate: 1.35M on Fable, about 450K each; 2.4M on Opus, about 400K each Blind Fable §4

  2. Checklist verifierSonnet×9, about 4 more to re-verify

    Reads the diff and the records; runs nothing. Eight items: the paths touched, no team test changed, the test's failure seen in its record before the fix, each library hunk in its piece's declarations, no cast round the checker, the S1 form, the ledger lines, the report. "Cheap, mechanical, high yield" Blind Fable §2, §3.

    Estimate: 0.9M, 13 at about 70K Blind Fable §4

  3. Semantic reviewerOpus×3: W, C-a, C-b

    Reads the Java and Scala diff beside the passages, and asks whether the code states exactly the rule: not wider, not narrower. Builds and runs nothing. Only these three, because "a three-vote adversarial panel is not [the right price], because the suites are a stronger refuter than a second reader" Blind Fable §3.

    Estimate: 0.4M, about 130K each Blind Fable §4

  4. Fixupthe implementer's tierabout 4, up to 2 more

    After a verifier's or a reviewer's issue: one more commit, test first. A re-verify follows a verifier's fixup. A library chain whose sites survive its distance run gets one more pass Blind Fable §2.

    Estimate: 0.7M, about 120K each, 2 on Fable and 4 on Opus Blind Fable §4

    Estimate: 0.35M, about 50K each Blind Fable §4

Not in it: a judge or ruling of any kind, and a review of the merged tree. A red gate, at a chain's end or on the merged tree, stops the run for you Blind Fable §2, §3.

Estimate: about 7.1M (5.5M to 8.5M): Fable about 1.6M, Opus 3.6M, Sonnet 1.9M. About 48 agents in its table, 46 in its text (40 to 52). About 13 hours, so "the run will meet the 13-hour stop once"; it resumes from the journal Blind Fable §4.

The blind Opus design

Shape: six implementers at once, each in its own worktree; then group runs in the background with three reviews beside them; a fix only where something was found; one gate on the merged tree; one commit Blind Opus §1.

Before the launch the coordinator, in about 15 minutes, builds or reuses the base, seeds six worktrees, and reuses the last gate result and per-site list when their code is the base's; otherwise the distance runs once, in the background Blind Opus §1.

The run log keeps rule 3, nothing built or run twice. It holds one line per build or run, keyed by a code id, a hash of the tree's source folders. An agent looks its command up first: "a finished result there is your result" Blind Opus §2.

Order: the six issued at once, longest first: N, G, C-infer, C-crash, W, C-decl. Batches, not a pipeline, so that a resume after the 13-hour stop replays the same calls Blind Opus §2.

  • Fable for C-infer only: "Its rows have a decided type that collides with the library route, and the place to fix row 593 is unmeasured. This is where a plausible but wrong repair is most likely and least visible to tests."

Estimate: about 4.3M on Opus (3.0M to 6.4M), up to 0.2M on Fable, about 0.1M on Sonnet. 10 Opus agents and the measure in the base case, about 12 expected, 17 at worst. About 9.5 to 10 hours (8 to 12) Opus §4.

The blind Fable design

Shape: four chains, one per piece, each in its own worktree on its own branch. A chain is a run of sub-pieces, each one implementer followed by a checker: nine in all, W one, C three, G two, N three. Why so fine: one

Before the chains a Sonnet base agent reuses the base build or builds it (about 200 s), seeds the four worktrees, and stops if the base's per-site list is missing Blind Fable §2. Order: the chains r

Tiers, its own choice Blind Fable §1:

  • Fable for W, C-a and C-b, "the three agents whose edit restates a rule every test depends on".
  • Opus for C-c and the five library repairers, "whose work is judgment over much reading"; also the reviewers, the integrator and the report writer.
  • Sonnet "for everything mechanical: verification by checklist, running suites, reading measurements, the S1-form check".
  1. ImplementerFable ×3Opus ×6×9

    Works in its chain's worktree after the sub-piece before it. Runs each test in the untouched worktree first and keeps the output as a record outside the repository; only then edits. W and C rebuild after their own edits (25 to 40 s); G and N build n

    Estimate: 1.35M on Fable, about 450K each; 2.4M on Opus, about 400K each Blind Fable §4

  2. Checklist verifierSonnet×9, about 4 more to re-verify

    Not in it: a judge or ruling of any kind, and a review of the merged tree. A red gate, at a chain's end or on the merged tree, stops the run for you Blind Fable §2, §3.

    Estimate: about 7.1M (5.5M to 8.5M): Fable about 1.6M, Opus 3.6M, Sonnet 1.9M. About 48 agents in its table, 46 in its text (40 to 52). About 13 hours, so "the run will meet the 13-hour stop once"; it resumes from the journal

The blind Opus design

Shape: six implementers at once, each in its own worktree; then group runs in the background with three reviews beside them; a fix only where something was found; one gate on the merged tree; one commit Blind Opus

Before the launch the coordinator, in about 15 minutes, builds or reuses the base, seeds six worktrees, and reuses the last gate result and per-site list when their code is the base's; otherwise the distance runs once, in the backg

The run log keeps rule 3, nothing built or run twice. It holds one line per build or run, keyed by a code id, a hash of the tree's source folders. An agent looks its command up first: "a finished result there is your result"

Order: the six issued at once, longest first: N, G, C-infer, C-crash, W, C-decl. Batches, not a pipeline, so that a resume after the 13-hour stop replays the same calls Blind Opus §2.
